prem-narrow-no-ovf.what: E2E_NARROW without |v| < OVF32. Known false: Turn 194 evaluated the IEEE shape at an input of 2^1000 and the result is not finite. Refused where the proof takes the premise

prem-sqrt-neg.what: E2E_SQRT32 without 0 <= x. False by Flocq's definition (Bsqrt of a negative number is NaN, not finite); not evaluated here. Refused where the proof takes the premise

prem-rsqrt-at-zero.text: "0 <= B2R b" while it is expected to have type
prem-rsqrt-at-zero.what: E2E_RSQRT32 with 0 <= x for 0 < x. False at 0 by Flocq's definition (1 / 0 is an infinity); refused where the proof gives the premise to ieee64's theorem

prem-hypot-no-range.what: E2E_HYPOT32 without its range premise. False (x * x overflows for a large x; ieee64's plant of the same name). Refused where the proof takes the premise

prem-exp-no-xmax.what: E2E_EXP32 without x <= XMAX. False (the squarings overflow for a large x). Refused where the proof takes the premise

concl-narrow-rd.what: E2E_NARROW with round down for round to nearest even. False wherever the two differ (T32 is proved); refused where T32's theorem no longer fits

concl-sqrt-of-x.what: E2E_SQRT32 says the result is a faithful rounding of x, not of sqrt x. False at x = 4 (the result is 2, argued from SQRT32, not evaluated); refused where SQRT32's theorem no longer fits

concl-rsqrt-is-sqrt.what: E2E_RSQRT32 says the result is a faithful rounding of sqrt x, not of 1 / sqrt x. False at x = 4 (argued); refused where RSQRT32's theorem no longer fits

concl-exp-correct.what: E2E_EXP32 claims the correctly rounded result, which the tier does not prove. NOT known false at any given input: refused only because the proof has no such theorem to apply

admitted-part.what: Compose.e2e_exp32 ends with Admitted (the last line of its proof moved to another lemma)

admitted-top.what: the top theorem compose_holds ends with Admitted

axiom-landing.what: that narrow's value is a finite binary32 number for every real input is an Axiom of Compose.v (false for a large input), used by E2E_NARROW's proof

other-statement.what: Compose.v states, under the name COMPOSE, the proposition True and proves that

guard.what: compose_holds from False, by a recursion whose termination check is switched off
